description: Canonical template-variable vocabulary for configuration snips. A variable is named for the semantic object it parameterizes, not for the textual position it occupies in a CLI statement.
aliasRule: A legacy variable name may be recorded as a global alias only when its semantic intent is unambiguous across known evidence. Ambiguous legacy names are recorded as scoped migration provenance instead.

INSTANCE_NAME.intent: Identity stem of a service instance.
INSTANCE_NAME.use: The routing-instance name, and the stem from which that service's derived object names are formed (for example PS-${INSTANCE_NAME}-IMPORT, PS-${INSTANCE_NAME}-EXPORT, ${INSTANCE_NAME}_RT, and a per-service community carrying the instance name itself). Do not introduce a separate variable for a name that is a deterministic derivative of this stem.

COLOR_COMMUNITY.use: Name of the community carrying the service transport-colour value. Referenced by policy or by service configuration that consumes that community.

migratedFrom.name: COLOR_COMM
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias. $COLOR_COMM denotes the same object in metro_as_a_service, which is frozen; it converges when that JVD is next revised. $COLOR_LIST in srv6_core_edge is a different object (a list of transport-class colour numbers) and is not related.

LOOPBACK_V4.use: The node's own lo0 IPv4. Retain this name even where the value also supplies a subfield of another object, such as the Administrator subfield of a Route Distinguisher.

LOOPBACK_ANYCAST_V4.use: A loopback address owned by more than one node, so the value repeats across the devices that share it.

LOOPBACK_SR_V4.intent: Segment Routing non-zero IPv4 loopback address.
LOOPBACK_SR_V4.use: The per-node loopback that carries an SR prefix-SID, distinct from the primary loopback. Naming records the intended construct; it does not assert that the address is currently instantiated on lo0.

RD.use: The entire RD is parameterized as one value.

RD_SUB_ADMIN.use: Only when the variable itself represents the RD Administrator subfield. If that subfield is supplied by a variable whose primary intent is broader (for example $LOOPBACK_V4), retain the broader variable.

RD_SUB_ASSIGNED.use: The assigned-number component when the RD components are independently parameterized.

migratedFrom.name: RD_ID
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: $RD_ID is semantically overloaded across the portfolio (Assigned Number subfield in metro_ethernet_business_services and broadband_edge; route-distinguisher-id seed in srv6_core_edge).

RT_AS.use: The administrator component of a route target, in any statement carrying one: vrf-target, vrf-target import, and a community members target:<administrator>:<assigned-number> definition. Service-scoped, not device-scoped — it varies between services on one node and is frequently not that node's own autonomous-system. Pair it with whichever variable supplies the Assigned Number.

migratedFrom.name: AS_LOCAL
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: every occurrence was the Administrator subfield of a vrf-target, while the name asserts a device-local AS that the bound values contradict.

migratedFrom.name: L3VPN_RT_AS
migratedFrom.note: Scoped migration provenance, not a global alias: the same Administrator subfield. The L3VPN qualifier named the constructs that used it, not a narrower semantic object.

RT_ID.use: The assigned-number component of a route target, independent of the variable supplying the Administrator.

notes: RD encoding (2-byte ASN, IPv4 address, or 4-byte ASN administrator) is per-occurrence evidence, not part of the variable name. Do not introduce $RD_ASN2, $RD_ASN4, or $RD_FIELD1 unless a construct genuinely requires that semantic distinction.
$RD_ID as the operand of route-distinguisher-id is a different semantic object and still awaits its own canonical name.
